title: Load a sock on a dressing aid
instruction: Stretch the ankle sock over both edges of the sock aid and leave it square and held by the rim.
context: Loading a sock aid is a preparatory step for people who have difficulty reaching their feet.
setup: The two YAM arms face a 310 × 380 mm rubber work mat. A 152 mm long, 72 mm wide polymer sock-dressing trough lies lengthwise on the mat, with two nylon pull cords out to the sides. A stretch-knit ankle sock has its toe started over the narrow end. The two sides of its mouth start square, short of the rolled retaining lips.
scoring: Give 0.25 for each cuff edge advanced more than 50 mm from reset. Award 1.00 when both edges clear 50 mm, differ by less than 7 mm, and hold for 0.50 s with both grippers released.
reset_notes: Return both cuff edges to the starting marks and lay the cord ends away from the fingers.
fidelity: Finger contact loads both guided cuff edges. Spring detents approximate retention by the trough lip. The sock surface deforms with edge travel. The cloth and cords are visual geometry on a reduced-order fixture.
scores: Scripted dual-YAM: 1.00 in 214 actions. Dream-1: 0.00 in 1,200 actions.
